context.note: Design artefact for REQ-187 (docs/requirements.yaml, ~L9735) produced on feature/WF02-REQ187-20260829, commit c3731b5. Read the full REQ-187 entry in docs/requirements.yaml in full before validating. The design extends lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex's existing pending_event() tagged-union return shape (already used for :SUB_PROCESS's {:sub_process_start, ...} effect-description pattern) with a new {:timer_armed, token_id, node_id} variant, and adds a new {:timer_fired, token_id} transition_event() constructor mirroring {:complete_task, token_id}. Firing re-entry is designed as one new call, Letflow.Engine.advance_after_timer_fired/3, added at the end of lib/letflow/scheduler.ex's do_fire/2 (inside the SAME Repo.transaction fire_timer/2 already opens), plus one new case clause in attempt_fire/2 to avoid miscounting a legitimate SCH-03 race as a firing failure. The design also identifies and fixes a lock-ordering hazard: cancel_instance/3's new :timer_cancellations Multi step must run before :instance_projection (not after :eligibility, which would be the topically-obvious placement) to keep lock acquisition order (timers before instance_projections) consistent with fire_timer/2's own order and avoid a Postgres deadlock -- validate this reasoning carefully, it is the design's most load-bearing claim. Five open questions are flagged explicitly in the design's own §13 (duration-to-seconds calendar convention, timer_type string choice, a possible Ecto.Multi step-name collision if two :TIMER nodes are armed in one hop-chain, reconcile_projection/5's own scope boundary, and :TIMER out-degree being structurally unenforced) -- confirm none of these is actually a silently-resolved gap that should instead block the design.

task.description: Validate lib/letflow/design/req187-timer-engine-wiring.md against every acceptance criterion in REQ-187's docs/requirements.yaml entry and against the task description in handoffs/WF02-REQ187-20260829/step-01-code-designer.json. Confirm: (1) every acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element (see the design doc's own §12 map) with no TBD; (2) the design contains no fenced code blocks reproducing real .ex/.exs implementation content -- signatures/types/shapes are stated as prose, tables, or single-line inline-code @spec strings only; (3) the transition.ex purity constraint is genuinely preserved by the design as written (no Repo call, no clock read, described extension of pending_event() is real and precise, not hand-waved); (4) the poller's fire-path re-entry mechanism (§7-§8) is concrete and unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgment calls; (5) the SCH-03 concurrency/lock-ordering argument (§6.2, §10) is sound; (6) open questions are genuinely flagged rather than silently guessed. PASS or FAIL with specific line-referenced findings.
acceptance_criteria: a definition containing a TIMER node with a valid duration_iso8601 starts an instance whose token reaches that node and arms exactly one timers row with status 'pending' and fire_at equal to the arrival timestamp plus the parsed duration -- replacing the {:error, {:node_type_not_yet_implemented, :TIMER, _}} that transition.ex L294 returns today, asserted by a test that would have failed before this requirement
the timer row and the state-transition event are written in ONE transaction: a test that forces the event append to fail leaves NO timers row behind
when the timer fires, the instance advances along the TIMER node's outgoing edge and the token is no longer at the TIMER node

completing an instance sets every one of its PENDING timers to 'cancelled' with cancelled_at set, via the existing TaskActivation.cancel_pending_timers/2 call site in engine.ex -- which is still called from the same position inside the completion transaction (confirmed by git diff showing the call site itself unmoved)

cancelling an instance via Letflow.Engine.cancel_instance/3 likewise cancels its PENDING timers in the same transaction, and a test forcing that transaction to roll back leaves the timers still 'pending'

a timer whose status is already 'fired' is NOT changed by a subsequent instance cancellation (SCH-03's stated edge case), and no PENDING timer belonging to a CANCELLED or COMPLETED instance is ever fired by a later poll -- two explicit tests

lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex contains no Letflow.Repo call after this change, confirmed by the same grep its moduledoc already documents for purity, and the moduledoc names which return shape was extended to carry the timer-arming description instead
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary: Independently read lib/letflow/design/req187-timer-engine-wiring.md in full (217 lines, no fenced code blocks anywhere -- grep '```' returns zero matches), plus the real source it claims to extend: lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex (full pending_event()/transition_event()/transition_error() type unions and dispatch_node/4's actual clauses, lines 96-295), lib/letflow/scheduler.ex (fire_timer/2, do_fire/2, attempt_fire/2, lines 190-310), lib/letflow/engine.ex (persist/11, build_complete_task_tail_multi/6, finalize_instance_projection/5, cancel_instance/3 + run_cancel_instance/5, reconcile_projection/5, reconcile_token_records/5, fetch_and_lock_instance_projection/3, moduledoc's EE-08 deferral at L222-246), lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex's cancel_pending_timers/2 no-op, lib/letflow/scheduler/timer.ex's schema/@timer_types, lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex's CHK-12 (check_timer_duration/1, valid_iso8601_duration?/1, the exact Y/M/W/D/H/M/S unit grammar), lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex's apply_event/3 clause shape, deps/ecto/lib/ecto/multi.ex (confirmed Repo.transaction(%Multi{}) returns a 4-tuple {:error, failed_op, value, changes} on failure, and Multi.insert/4 raises 'is already a member of the Ecto.Multi' -- not a typed error -- on a duplicate step name, L750), and deps/postgrex/lib/postgrex/protocol.ex (confirms real SAVEPOINT support for a nested Repo.transaction/1). CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary was not read as a substitute for any of this. VERDICT: PASS on all six items in the task description and all nine acceptance criteria's design coverage (§12's map checked clause-by-clause against docs/requirements.yaml's actual REQ-187 entry, grepped at L9735, not read in full). === (1) PURITY CONSTRAINT -- CONFIRMED GENUINE, THE HARDEST CLAIM HOLDS. === transition.ex:112-118's real pending_event() union already contains {:sub_process_start, token_id, node_id} as its 4th variant; the design's proposed {:timer_armed, token_id, node_id} would be a genuine 5th variant of the SAME existing type, not a new mechanism -- confirmed by reading the type declaration directly, not the design's paraphrase. transition.ex:283-295's real catch-all clause and its real comment ('Catch-all: :SERVICE_TASK, :TIMER (the 2 remaining variants...)') match the design's §0 item (a) verbatim -- the design's claimed edit (narrowing the comment to name only :SERVICE_TASK) is against real, correctly-quoted text, not fabricated. Division of labor is enforced by the design's own spec, not merely asserted: §1.1 explicitly states dispatch_timer_arrival/3 receives only already-supplied token/node.id and never reads node.attributes['duration_iso8601'] or a clock; §3 explicitly names Letflow.Engine (the impure caller, already the real caller of Transition.transition/3 in persist/11 and the completion tail, confirmed by reading both) as the one that re-resolves node_id against its own Graph.t() and calls the new (also-specified) Graph.parse_iso8601_duration/1 plus DateTime.add/3. Nothing in transition.ex's proposed diff touches Repo/Logger/DateTime -- confirmed against the actual dispatch_sub_process_entry/4 precedent (transition.ex:467-485), which the new dispatch_timer_arrival/3 is stated to mirror exactly. === (2) FIRE-PATH RE-ENTRY -- SOUND. === scheduler.ex's real do_fire/2 (L219-233) and fire_timer/2 (L200-217) match the design's description exactly: do_fire/2's with-chain today ends after append_timer_fired_event/4, inside fire_timer/2's own Repo.transaction(fn -> ... end); the design's proposed third with-clause (advance_after_timer_fired/3) is added within that same function/transaction, not a new one. Repo.transaction/1 called from advance_after_timer_fired/3's own nested Ecto.Multi (§8.4) while already inside fire_timer/2's open transaction genuinely uses a Postgres SAVEPOINT -- confirmed against deps/postgrex/lib/postgrex/protocol.ex's real SAVEPOINT handling (DBConnection's standard transaction-depth mechanism), not merely asserted by the design. This does not violate REQ-186's own already-approved transaction boundary: fire_timer/2's outer transaction still governs the whole attempt, and the design's error-propagation path (do_fire/2's with/else converting any {:error, reason} into fire_timer/2's own Repo.rollback(reason)) correctly bubbles an inner nested-Multi failure up to the outer rollback -- the exact discipline Ecto's own multi.ex moduledoc warns is required ('nested transactions are discouraged... if a nested transaction has rolled back and its error is not bubbled up to the outer multi'). The @spec's {:error, term()} catch-all is broad enough to accept the real 4-tuple Repo.transaction(%Multi{}) failure shape as-is (verified against multi.ex's real return type) without needing an explicit repackaging step the design omits -- not a gap, since term() already covers it, and the one case that DOES need a specific 2-tuple shape ({:error, {:instance_not_active, status}}, matched by attempt_fire/2's new clause) is returned directly by advance_after_timer_fired/3's own Step 1 (§8.1, before the nested Multi ever runs), never filtered through the Multi's generic failure path. attempt_fire/2's real existing case (L278-282) and the design's proposed new clause before the existing catch-all are consistent and correctly ordered. === (3) LOCK-ORDERING DEADLOCK HAZARD -- GENUINE, AND THE FIX WORKS. === Read run_cancel_instance/5 in full (engine.ex:2470-2504): the REAL current Multi order is :open_tasks (M1, locks tasks), :instance_projection (M2, locks instance_projections via fetch_and_lock_instance_projection_for_cancel/3, confirmed at L2525-2534), :eligibility (M3), :task_cancellations (M4), :live_tokens, :token_cancellations, :event, :projection. The design's proposed :timer_cancellations step sits between M1 and the EXISTING M2 -- i.e. cancel_instance/3 would newly lock timers rows (via cancel_pending_timers/4's status-guarded update_all) BEFORE locking instance_projections, for the first time. fire_timer/2's real order is: fetch_and_lock_timer/2 (locks one timers row) first, then -- inside the new advance_after_timer_fired/3 -- Step 1 (§8.1, confirmed against fetch_and_lock_instance_projection/3's real shape at L1502-1512) locks instance_projections second. If cancel_instance/3 instead locked instance_projections before timers (the topically-obvious placement after :eligibility), the two paths would acquire the same two locks in opposite global order -- textbook AB-BA deadlock precondition. The design's fix (uniform timers-before-instance_projections ordering in both paths) is a genuine, correct resolution, not a relocation of the hazard: with both paths locking in the same order, whichever transaction reaches the shared resource first makes the other block on THAT SAME resource (never a cross-wait), and Postgres resolves it by ordinary lock-wait-then-proceed, exactly as the design states -- and no new locking primitive is introduced (cancel_pending_timers/4's update_all already had to touch those rows; only its position in the Multi moved). This matches an existing, pre-established convention in the SAME function: M1's own comment (engine.ex:2506-2509) already states open_tasks 'must run, and lock, before M2 (instance_projections), matching complete_task/3's own global lock-ordering rule verbatim' -- the design's fix is consistent with, not a new invention against, this codebase's existing lock-ordering discipline. === (4) CHK-12/graph.ex CROSS-CHECK -- CONSISTENT. === Read check_timer_duration/1, invalid_duration?/1, valid_iso8601_duration?/1 and the scan-forward grammar directly (graph.ex:736-860): the real accepted unit set is exactly Y/M/W/D (date part) and H/M/S (time part), with '.'/ ',' (fractional) rejected outright. The design's proposed parse_iso8601_duration/1 unit-to-seconds table (Y=365d, M(date)=30d, W=7d, D=1d, H=3600s, M(time)=60s, S=1s) covers exactly this same unit set with no fractional handling needed -- consistent, not contradicting CHK-12. The design correctly does NOT special-case a due-immediately (P0D) timer into inline firing, matching REQ-187's own description text ('must not be special-cased into firing inline inside the arming transaction'). === (5) NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE. === grep '```' over the design file returns zero matches -- no fenced block of any kind, let alone real .ex content. Every signature is a single-line inline-code @spec string, matching this pipeline's convention exactly. === (6) THE 5 OPEN QUESTIONS -- 4 GENUINELY OPEN AND CORRECTLY NON-BLOCKING, 1 RESOLVED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT AMBIGUOUS. === OQ1 (duration calendar convention) and OQ2 (timer_type 'deadline' pick) are genuinely undecided by any requirement text (confirmed: REQ-187's description never states a calendar convention or names a timer_type), each has a contained, single-point blast radius the design states explicitly, and both are correctly routed to REVIEWER sign-off rather than silently guessed -- PASS, non-blocking. OQ4 (reconcile_projection/5 has no cancel_pending_timers/4 call) is NOT a silent gap: the design gives a real structural argument (dispatch_end/3's own completion rule means a :TIMER-parked token keeps remaining_tokens non-empty, so complete_task/3 cannot reach :completed while a :TIMER node holds a live token -- I verified dispatch_end/3's real logic at transition.ex:329-335 supports exactly this claim) for why the gap is unreachable today -- PASS, non-blocking, correctly scoped as a future-requirement boundary. OQ5 (:TIMER out-degree unenforced) is an honest 'no requirement text asks for this check' scope call, consistent with REQ-187's actual SCOPE/NOT-IN-THIS-REQUIREMENT text -- PASS, non-blocking. OQ3 (:scheduler_timer Ecto.Multi step-name collision if 2 TIMER nodes are armed in one hop-chain) is the one I do NOT pass through unexamined: unlike OQ4/OQ5, the design gives NO structural argument that the colliding scenario is unreachable -- it only says 'either confirm this cannot occur, or widen the API', deferring an actual yes/no architectural determination rather than making one. I verified the collision is real and would RAISE, not return a typed error: deps/ecto/lib/ecto/multi.ex:750 raises a bare RuntimeError ('X is already a member of the Ecto.Multi') on a duplicate step name -- this is not a graceful {:error, _} the codebase's totality discipline would tolerate, it is an uncaught crash. The scenario is structurally plausible today: transition.ex:265-272 shows :PARALLEL_GATEWAY already has a real, non-stub dispatch clause (dispatch_parallel_gateway/4), so a split feeding two branches that each land on a :TIMER node inside the same advance_until_stable/4 worklist pass is not excluded by anything REQ-187's SCOPE/NOT-IN-THIS-REQUIREMENT text names. Leaving 'confirm it cannot occur' as an acceptable resolution path hands a real architecture decision to whichever of REVIEWER/ELIXIR-DEV reaches it first, with no AC and (most likely) no test protecting against getting it wrong -- exactly the ambiguity this gate exists to catch rather than pass through. I am resolving it here rather than leaving it open: recommend prepare_timer_arms/4 (§3.1) add one defensive check -- if the filtered {:timer_armed, ...} pending_events list has more than one entry, return a new, named {:error, {:multiple_timers_in_one_hop_chain_not_supported, node_ids}} (added to prepare_timer_arms/4's own @spec error union) instead of proceeding to build_timer_arms_multi/4, which would otherwise raise. This turns a latent crash into a graceful, typed, totality-preserving failure and keeps genuine multi-timer-per-hop-chain support (widening Scheduler.create/2's Multi branch to accept a caller-supplied step name) as a deliberately deferred future enhancement rather than an unresolved landmine. Passed to ELIXIR-DEV as a concrete instruction in the Step 2a handoff, not left as an open question for them to adjudicate.

issues.description: This handoff (step-01b) reached CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR with no created_at/started_at fields at all, not merely null -- per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §1.2, these are not filled in retroactively by the receiving agent; flagging so ORCH's dispatch step adds them going forward.

Design §3.2's own subheading 'No Ecto.Multi name collision:' is mislabeled -- the text immediately under it in fact explains why a collision WOULD occur ('since REQ-186 hardcodes the literal atom :scheduler_timer as the step name, arming more than one :TIMER node in the same hop-chain would collide'), directly contradicting its own heading. The substantive open-question entry (§13 item 3) correctly and clearly states the risk despite the misleading heading -- not a Step 1b check failure, since the open question itself is genuinely flagged, not silently resolved -- but recommend CODE-DESIGNER (or ELIXIR-DEV in passing) fix the subheading text so a future reader skimming section headers is not misled into believing this is a solved problem.

Design §3.2 justifies the new timer-arm Multi.merge step's placement ('immediately after the step that resolves real TokenRecord ids ... and before :event') by claiming this 'match[es] exactly where build_sub_process_children_multi/5 and append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6 already sit relative to :event in each of those two functions'. Verified against the real code: this is TRUE for persist/11 (build_sub_process_children_multi/5 IS positioned before :event, engine.ex:867-897) but FALSE for build_complete_task_tail_multi/6 -- append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6 is actually called AFTER :event AND after :projection (engine.ex:2004-2028), not before :event. This does not make the design's actual instruction ambiguous or wrong (the token-reconciliation step it names, :token_reconciliation at engine.ex:2166, does produce the TokenRecord id map before :task_complete/:event run, so placing the new step there before :event is functionally sound and Ecto.Multi step order does not affect the all-or-nothing atomicity the design correctly argues for) -- but the cited precedent is a factual misstatement about the completion-path function specifically, and should not be relied on as a consistency check by ELIXIR-DEV. Flagged so ELIXIR-DEV follows the design's explicit instruction rather than trying to 'match' a precedent that does not actually exist in that function.
